question: Who hosted the 2011 ODI cricket world cup?
solution:
The correct answer is __**India, Sri Lanka, Bangladesh**__

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• The 2011 ODI Cricket World Cup was **co-hosted by India, Sri Lanka, and Bangladesh**.
 
• This was the **tenth edition** of the Cricket World Cup, and it was the third time it was held in the Indian subcontinent.
 
• India went on to win the tournament, marking their second World Cup victory, the first being in 1983.
 
• The final match was held at the **Wankhede Stadium in Mumbai, India**, where India defeated Sri Lanka.
 
• The tournament featured a total of **14 teams** competing in 49 matches.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• The 2011 Cricket World Cup saw the use of the **Decision Review System (DRS)** for the first time in a World Cup.
 
• It was the first time that Bangladesh co-hosted the World Cup, although India and Sri Lanka had previously co-hosted in 1987 and 1996.
 
• The tournament was notable for the **high-scoring matches** and the performances of several key players, including India's Sachin Tendulkar and Yuvraj Singh, who was named the Player of the Tournament.
 
• The mascot for the 2011 World Cup was **Stumpy**, a young elephant.
 
• The official song of the 2011 Cricket World Cup was "**De Ghuma Ke**", composed by the trio of Shankar–Ehsaan–Loy.
